gen-dafont-disorder-gf-aldrich: Disorder sprawls with tall, widely spaced lowercase and no swelling where curves meet stems, while Aldrich follows in modern sans with a single thick thread of line. Raw against tidy.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-alexandria: Alexandria takes the body, a clean sans with a gaping c and a tall build with short stems, under Disorder's poured-ink heading. Alexandria keeps a long page moving smoothly, since its letters stay open and unfussy.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-amiko: Disorder draws its tall, scattered letters with a marker-like constant line. It handles loud, ragged headings best, whereas Amiko, a sans-serif with outward-pointing terminals, handles steady text.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-bangla: Anek Bangla is a plain sans with wide s curves and a short climb from midline to ascender, giving the text a approachable feel. But Disorder, with no thick-thin modulation at all, does the shouting while the body does the explaining.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-devanagari: Wire-bent and restless, Disorder stretches its oversized lowercase across every word. Anek Devanagari, a sans with distinctly open letter mouths, can sit well below it, so try the heading much larger than the text.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati has lowercase that rivals its capitals and a gaping c, which makes the sans text feel friendly. And Disorder, with curves as thick as its straight stems, can go large, with the body kept noticeably smaller.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Scrappy and unshaded, Disorder has no calligraphic contrast to guide the eye. Anek Gurmukhi, a sans-serif with big open counters and generous round curves, steps in so the text stays easy to follow.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-kannada: Anek Kannada reads modern and squared-off, with a high x-height and terminals that stop far from the stem. Yet Disorder, one stroke thickness everywhere, is the one that supplies the chaos above it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-anek-latin: Disorder looks flat-lined and untamed, with no swelling along any curve. Anek Latin, a sans-serif with lowercase nearly reaching the capitals and letters held open, would carry paragraphs without tiring.
